Package edu.cnu.mdi.splot.fit

Class CubicSpline

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.splot.fit.CubicSpline
All Implemented Interfaces:
Evaluator
public class CubicSpline extends Object implements Evaluator
Natural cubic spline interpolator over tabulated data (x[i], y[i]).

This class precomputes the natural cubic spline second derivatives and can:

  • Interpolate values value(double).
  • Build an approximate derivative spline via numeric differentiation derivative().
  • Find roots in a range using bracket-and-refine utilities findRoots(double, double).
  • Find maxima in a range by locating zeros of the first derivative and testing the second derivative findXValsOfMaxima(double, double).

Spline details

The spline is "natural": the second derivative is forced to be zero at the endpoints. Between consecutive knots x[i] <= x <= x[i+1], the interpolant is a cubic polynomial chosen so that y, y' and y'' are continuous across knots.

Requirements

  • x[] and y[] must be non-null, same length, and length >= 2.
  • x[] must be strictly increasing (no duplicates).

Out-of-range evaluation

If x is outside [x[0], x[n-1]], this implementation clamps to the nearest endpoint (returns y[0] or y[n-1]).

    • derivative

      public CubicSpline derivative()
      Obtain a cubic spline that approximates the derivative of this spline by numeric differentiation at the knots, then spline-interpolating those derivative samples.

      The derivatives are estimated using:

      • Centered differences for interior points
      • One-sided differences for the endpoints
      This is robust and simple. If you need an analytic derivative of the spline itself, you could compute it directly from the spline coefficients; this method instead builds a new spline based on sampled slopes at knots.
      Returns:
      a new CubicSpline approximating dy/dx

    • findRoots

      public double[] findRoots(double xmin, double xmax)
      Find the roots of the interpolated function in a range.

      This method:

      1. Uses Zbrak#zbrak(UniVarRealValueFun, double, double, int) to bracket sign changes.
      2. For each bracketed interval, refines the root using RtSafe#rtsafe(UniVarRealValueFun, double, double, double).

      Dependencies: This assumes your project provides Numerical-Recipes-like helpers: UniVarRealValueFun, Zbrak, and RtSafe.

      Parameters:
      xmin - the min value of the search range
      xmax - the max value of the search range
      Returns:
      an array of roots (sorted ascending), or null if none are found
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if xmax <= xmin

    • findXValsOfMaxima

      public Point2D.Double[] findXValsOfMaxima(double xmin, double xmax)
      Find the (x, y) values of the maxima of the interpolated function in a given range.

      Implementation strategy:

      1. Compute a spline approximation to the first derivative.
      2. Find its roots (critical points) in [xmin, xmax].
      3. Compute a spline approximation to the second derivative.
      4. Keep only critical points where the second derivative is negative (local maxima).
      5. Return the corresponding (x, f(x)) pairs, sorted by descending y if there is more than one.
      Parameters:
      xmin - the min value of the range
      xmax - the max value of the range
      Returns:
      an array of maxima points, or null if none are found
